agency.name: Bureau of Drug and Alcohol Services, New Hampshire Department of Health and Human Services

narrAffiliate.name: New Hampshire Coalition of Recovery Residences (NHCORR)

narrNote: NHCORR appears on NARR's official affiliate list and states it is the sole entity authorized by NARR to certify recovery houses in New Hampshire. See notes for a separate state-designation change.
notes: SPLIT-ROLE WARNING: NHCORR remains New Hampshire's NARR state affiliate (per NARR's official list, which governs this field), but under a state designation letter dated December 3, 2024, the New Hampshire Partnership for Recovery Residences (NHPRR, operated by Growth Partners LLC) describes itself as the state-designated certifying agency; NH DHHS's recovery housing page still describes NHCORR as state-designated. Confirm with the funder/referral source which certificate they recognize. Agency identity from SAMHSA's SSA directory (Bureau of Drug and Alcohol Services, NH DHHS); the BDAS page on dhhs.nh.gov was fetched, but published no bureau phone, so agency.phone is null. The NH Rapid Response Access Point (operated by Carelon on behalf of NH DHHS, 24/7 call/text/chat) is documented on the linked NH DHHS children's behavioral health resources page and promoted by DHHS via nh988.com. medicaidSud is null: NH Medicaid covers a full SUD continuum through its managed-care plans (NH Healthy Families, WellSense Health Plan, AmeriHealth Caritas NH), but DHHS publishes no single member-facing Medicaid SUD benefits page; no commercial substitute was used. countyDirectory is null: NH organizes behavioral health through 10 community mental health centers and regional public health networks, not a county directory.
